_note: The parameter catalogue for this corpus: every number a statute did not state, with its unit (the corpus's own units are accepted and scaled by the decoder), the convention its value comes from and its source. It starts empty: the plan decides which parameters exist and proposes each with a provisional value, and the harness enters the proposal here marked `proposed` (run, iteration, node) until the operator reviews it by removing the marker or changing the value; the doctor lists every unreviewed proposal. The operator-authored list this file carried before any law was planned is kept, out of the pipeline's path, under readings/legacy/. Figures the law states are literals on the rule's span, never entries here.

params.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
params.convention: halt-detection convention: a sampled speed is never exactly zero, and a speed at or below the resolution of ordinary speed measurement counts as no movement; the value bounds the measurement noise, not the duration of the halt
params.source: stopped-vehicle detection practice in traffic-engineering field measurement (speed-sensor resolution class)

params.name: p.stop_place_tolerance
params.convention: stop-line placement tolerance: the distance within which a halted vehicle counts as halted at a marked place, covering the vehicle's reference-point offset and the survey tolerance of the marking
params.source: MUTCD stop-line placement practice and survey tolerance for pavement markings

params.name: p.intersection_view_distance
params.convention: intersection (approach) sight distance: the along-way view needed to see traffic approaching on the intersecting way at its design speed, from the place at which a driver may proceed
params.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance, case B (stop-controlled approach)

params.name: p.stop_approach_lookback
params.convention: approach look-back: the distance travelled before entering the intersection within which the required halt must be found; it bounds the stretch of the approach the rule searches and is measured in path travelled, as the words measure the halt by place on the approach
params.source: stop-sign compliance measurement practice (approach-zone length used in field studies)

params.name: p.speed_resolution
params.convention: source resolution: the speed below which a measured speed does not stand clear of zero; it names only the source's resolution and states no legal threshold
params.source: speed-sensor resolution class of ordinary trace sources

params.name: p.following_reach
params.convention: following reach: the longitudinal distance within which a leading road user is the one being followed, taken from the span over which a car-following interaction is identified at highway speeds; it relates two road users and states no adequacy
params.source: car-following and platoon-identification practice in traffic-flow measurement

params.name: p.following_alignment_tolerance
params.convention: heading-alignment tolerance: the angle within which two headings count as aligned, absorbing lane curvature and heading noise over a sampled trajectory
params.source: same-direction classification practice in trajectory processing

params.name: p.headway_dry
params.convention: time-headway convention (the two-second rule): the gap is the distance the follower covers at its own speed during a headway time that absorbs the driver's perception-reaction time and a braking margin; dry surface
params.source: driver-handbook two-second rule; AASHTO perception-reaction time of 2.5 s for braking

params.name: p.headway_wet
params.convention: the same time-headway convention with the wet-surface braking factor, which lengthens the braking share of the headway
params.source: driver-handbook wet-surface following advice; wet-pavement friction factors of the stopping-distance model

params.name: p.headway_ice
params.convention: the same time-headway convention with the icy or snow-covered braking factor
params.source: winter-driving following advice; ice and packed-snow friction factors of the stopping-distance model

params.name: p.closing_time
params.convention: closing-speed allowance: the time over which the speed difference between follower and leader is allowed to close the gap, so that a faster follower owes more space than a matched one
params.source: time-to-collision surrogate-safety practice in car-following analysis

params.name: p.traffic_gap_increment
params.convention: density increment: the additional space owed for each road user of the traffic on the highway within the reach about the subject, so that the bound rises as the traffic thickens
params.source: headway-density relations of the Highway Capacity Manual's level-of-service bands

params.name: p.traffic_reach
params.convention: reach of the traffic about the subject: the centre distance within which another road user counts as part of the traffic upon the highway the subject is on; it relates road users and states no adequacy
params.source: local-density window used in traffic-flow measurement

params.name: p.lane_change_window
params.convention: manoeuvre-recognition window: the stretch of time behind the observation within which the lane the road user came from is looked for, taken from the observed duration of a lane change from the first steering input to settling in the new lane. It names only how far back the earlier lane membership is sought and sets no standard of conduct.
params.source: lane-change duration studies of naturalistic driving (median about 4 s, from first steering input to settling)

params.name: p.lane_change_horizon
params.convention: gap-acceptance horizon: the time ahead over which the closest approach of the subject and another road user is computed under constant velocities, taken as the time a lane change occupies the space between the two lanes.
params.source: lane-change duration studies; the same source as the recognition window, taken at its crossing phase

params.name: p.lane_change_clearance
params.convention: gap-acceptance clearance: the distance between two bodies below which a lane change cannot be made with safety, taken as a passenger-car design vehicle's length so that the entering body does not come within a vehicle length of another.
params.source: AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, passenger car design vehicle length

params.name: p.lane_change_yaw_rate
params.convention: manoeuvre-detection tolerance: the magnitude of yaw rate above which the body counts as steering rather than holding its course, set above the yaw of following an ordinary highway bend and above heading noise, and naming only the resolution at which turning is told from running straight.
params.source: the yaw rate of a vehicle on a highway curve at the design radius, below which steering is not distinguishable from course keeping

params.name: p.lateral_offset_resolution
params.convention: source resolution: the magnitude of signed lateral offset below which a region does not stand clear of the road user's own axis, naming only the positional resolution of the source and the half-width of a painted or kerbed boundary; it sets no standard of conduct and no required separation.
params.source: the lateral positional accuracy of ordinary mapped road geometry and vehicle positioning (decimetre class)

params.name: p.opening_reach
params.convention: reach of an opening: the distance from a road user's body outline to an opening or crossover in a dividing structure within which the crossing counts as made through that opening rather than elsewhere on the highway. It is taken from the length of a median crossover, so a vehicle standing in or immediately at the opening is covered and one crossing the barrier well away from it is not.
params.source: the typical length of a median crossover or emergency crossing on a divided highway

params.name: p.yield_approach_speed
params.convention: yield-controlled approach convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle approaching a yield sign can give way to traffic on the intersecting way and halt before entering it within the view the approach affords
params.source: AASHTO Green Book yield-controlled approach speeds; MUTCD application of the yield sign

params.name: p.cautious_speed
params.convention: stopping-sight-distance model: the speed from which a vehicle can halt within the view an intersection approach affords
params.source: the same value this iteration's earlier batch proposed for NRS_484B_250_4_o2

params.name: p.yield_clearance
params.convention: gap-acceptance clearance: the centre-to-centre distance at closest approach below which the two vehicles' paths conflict and the one owing the duty has taken the precedence
params.source: the same value this iteration's earlier batch proposed for NRS_484B_250_4_o2

params.name: p.yield_horizon
params.convention: conflict horizon for gap acceptance: the time ahead over which the closest approach of two bodies is computed under constant velocities
params.source: the same value this iteration's earlier batch proposed for NRS_484B_250_4_o2

params.name: p.hazard_horizon
params.convention: immediate-hazard horizon: the time ahead within which an approaching vehicle's arrival makes it an immediate hazard to a vehicle crossing the junction
params.source: the same value this iteration's earlier batch proposed for NRS_484B_253_o1

params.name: p.hazard_clearance
params.convention: immediate-hazard clearance: the centre-to-centre distance at closest approach at or below which an approaching vehicle counts as so close as to be an immediate hazard
params.source: the same value this iteration's earlier batch proposed for NRS_484B_253_o1

params.name: p.approach_lane_window
params.convention: approach look-back: the stretch of time behind the observation within which the approach lane a road user came to the junction on is looked for
params.source: the same value this iteration's earlier batch proposed for NRS_484B_250_1

params.name: p.speed_dry
params.convention: surface-braking convention, baseline: the free-flow speed that is reasonable on a dry surface in daylight on an ordinary two-lane highway, before any reduction for surface, light, sight, width or traffic
params.source: design speeds of rural two-lane highways in highway design practice

params.name: p.speed_wet
params.convention: the same surface-braking convention with the wet-surface braking factor, which lengthens the braking share of the stopping distance
params.source: wet-pavement friction factors of the stopping-distance model

params.name: p.speed_ice
params.convention: the same surface-braking convention with the icy or snow-covered braking factor
params.source: icy-pavement friction factors of the stopping-distance model

params.name: p.speed_dark
params.convention: night allowance: the baseline speed in darkness, at which a vehicle can stop within the length of road its own lamps show
params.source: headlamp-range and night stopping-sight-distance practice

params.name: p.sight_clearance_time
params.convention: stopping-sight-distance convention: the time within which the vehicle must be able to come to a halt inside the distance it can see, so that the bound is the visible distance divided by this time
params.source: perception-reaction plus braking times of the stopping-sight-distance model

params.name: p.reference_lane_width
params.convention: lane-width reference: the standard lane width at which the baseline speed is owed in full, the deficit below it costing speed
params.source: standard lane widths in highway design practice

params.name: p.width_penalty_time
params.convention: lane-width allowance: the time in which the vehicle covers the missing width, so that each metre of lane width short of the reference costs the speed covered in that time
params.source: narrow-lane speed reductions in highway design practice

params.name: p.traffic_speed_decrement
params.convention: traffic-density allowance: the speed the bound falls by for each road user of the traffic on the same highway within the reach, so that the bound falls as the stream thickens
params.source: speed-flow relations of traffic flow practice

params.name: p.corner_turn_window
params.convention: turn-recognition window: the stretch of time behind the observation within which the heading the road user turned from is looked for, taken from the duration of a low-speed turning movement at a junction, from the first steering input to settling on the new course. It names only how far back the earlier heading is sought and sets no standard of conduct.
params.source: geometric design practice for low-speed turning movements at intersections

params.name: p.corner_min_heading_change
params.convention: corner-turn recognition: the magnitude of heading change at or above which a movement counts as having gone round a corner, taken from the angle between two ways that join, in the words of DEF-NRS-484A-105, "at, or approximately at, right angles", less the margin by which approximately right-angled junctions and sampled headings depart from a quarter turn. It names the resolution at which going round a corner is told from backing straight, not how sharp a corner must be to matter.
params.source: the junction geometry the posted definition of an intersection describes, with the heading tolerance of sampled trajectories

params.name: p.turn_window
params.convention: Turn-recognition window: the stretch of time behind the observation within which the heading a road user turned from is looked for. It is taken from the time a vehicle takes to carry out a turn at a junction or a reversal of direction on a roadway, from the first steering input to settling on the new heading, and it is long enough to cover a turning accomplished in more than one movement, as the definition of a U-turn requires. It names only how far back the earlier heading is sought and sets no standard of conduct.
params.source: Observed turn durations at junctions and of multi-movement turns at low speed (intersection-manoeuvre timing studies underlying junction clearance intervals).

params.name: p.u_turn_min_heading_change
params.convention: Reversal-of-direction band, lower edge: a sampled heading never reverses exactly, so this names how near a half turn counts as proceeding in the opposite direction. It is set far enough below a half turn to absorb the heading noise and the sampling of a turning made at low speed, and far enough above a quarter turn that an ordinary turn at a junction does not reach it.
params.source: Heading-integration tolerance over sampled trajectories, taken with the quarter-turn and half-turn geometry of road manoeuvres.

params.name: p.u_turn_max_heading_change
params.convention: Reversal-of-direction band, upper edge: it keeps a road user that goes on turning - round a roundabout, round a block - from counting as having reversed its direction, and is set as far above a half turn as the lower edge is below it.
params.source: The same heading-integration tolerance, applied symmetrically about a half turn.

params.name: p.left_turn_min_heading_change
params.convention: Left-turn band, lower edge: the magnitude of signed heading change to the left at or above which a movement counts as a turn to the left rather than a drift, a lane change or an ordinary bend held. It is set below a quarter turn, since junctions meet at angles that are only approximately right, and well above the heading change of a lane change.
params.source: The angles at which highways join (approximately, but not exactly, right angles, as the definition of an intersection allows) together with the heading change of an ordinary lane change.

params.name: p.left_turn_max_heading_change
params.convention: Left-turn band, upper edge: it keeps a road user that goes on turning past a quarter turn towards a reversal of direction from counting as having made a left turn, and is set at the midpoint between a quarter turn and the lower edge of the reversal band, so that the two bands do not overlap and a turning falls in at most one of them.
params.source: The same quarter-turn and half-turn geometry, with the reversal band's lower edge.

params.name: p.crossing_entry_lookback
params.convention: crossing look-back: the stretch of path behind a halt within which an earlier overlap of a crossing shows the halt to have been made after the vehicle entered that crossing rather than before it. It is taken from the ground between an entry into a marked crossing and a halt placed within the placement tolerance beyond it - the length of the crossing, the length of a design vehicle, the placement tolerance, and one sampling interval at an ordinary approach speed - so that the entry is found where it occurred and no earlier conduct of the approach is reached. It names only how far back the entry is sought and sets no standard of conduct.
params.source: crosswalk width and passenger-car design-vehicle length of the geometric design conventions, with the stop-line placement tolerance of `p.stop_place_tolerance` and the sampling interval of an ordinary trace at an urban approach speed

params.name: p.mount_proximity
params.convention: sign-assembly mounting convention: the distance from a sign's face, taken on each world axis, within which a beacon head counts as mounted with that sign. It is taken from the dimensions of a roadside sign assembly and the offset at which a pair of beacon lamps is fixed above or beside the sign face it serves, so that a head on the same post or the same mast arm is covered and a head at the next installation along the road is not. It names how close a head must stand to belong to a sign's assembly and states no standard of conduct and no required separation.
params.source: roadside sign and beacon mounting practice (MUTCD sign-assembly and beacon-mounting dimensions)

params.name: p.signal_lookback
params.convention: Signalling-interval convention: the stretch of time behind the observation at which a movement is recognized within which a turn signal given for that movement is looked for. It covers the interval a driver is expected to signal before beginning the movement together with the time the movement itself occupies, so that a signal duly given before the body begins to cross is still found when the movement is recognized; it names only where the signal is looked for and states no standard of conduct.
params.source: Driver-licensing signalling guidance (a continuous signal over the last stretch of road before the movement, commonly 100 feet, which is some two to three seconds at ordinary highway speeds) together with observed lane-change durations from the first steering input to settling in the new lane.

params.name: p.following_heading_cosine
params.convention: Heading-alignment convention, stated as a cosine: the cosine of the largest angle between two headings at which the two bodies still count as travelling in one line, so that the bend of a lane and the heading noise of a sampled trajectory are absorbed without admitting a body that points across the lane. The value is the cosine of the angle the catalogue states in degrees as p.following_alignment_tolerance, and it is stated as a ratio because rel.same_direction's tolerance is 'the cosine of the largest angle allowed, a ratio between -1 and 1'. It names a resolution and no standard of conduct.
params.source: the heading dispersion of vehicle trajectories held within a lane on ordinary highway alignments, as car-following trajectory studies record it

params.name: p.junction_approach_reach
params.convention: Entrance-of-intersection reach: the ground distance from an intersection region within which a vehicle's body counts as standing at that intersection's entrance rather than back along its approach. It is taken from the geometry of an entrance - the setback of a clearly marked stop line from the near-side crosswalk, the width of that crosswalk between the line and the edge of the intersection, and the offset of a vehicle's body outline - so that a halt made at the line, before the near-side crosswalk, or at the point nearest the intersection is found at the junction it was made for, and a cessation made further back along the approach is not. It names where a halt counts as made for this junction and states no standard of conduct and no required separation.
params.source: Stop-line and crosswalk placement at signalised junctions: the marked stop line is set back from the crosswalk, and the crosswalk from the intersection edge, by a few metres each, which with a design vehicle's body offset bounds the ground between a vehicle halted at the entrance and the intersection region.

params.name: p.body_offset_resolution
params.convention: source resolution: the magnitude of an offset between two road users' reference points below which the one does not stand clear of the other along an axis of the subject's frame. It names only the positional resolution of a tracked reference point and states no standard of conduct and no required separation.
params.source: the positional accuracy of ordinary vehicle tracking from a mapped scene graph or an instrumented trace, which resolves a reference point to a few tenths of a metre

params.name: p.single_file_reach
params.convention: single-file convention: the lateral offset between the reference points of two road users within which the one travels in the line of the other rather than beside it. It is taken from the width of a passenger-car design vehicle, so that two bodies in one line of travel, whose reference points differ laterally by no more than a body width, are covered, while two bodies in neighbouring lanes a standard lane width apart are not. It names when one body is in the other's line and states no standard of conduct and no required separation.
params.source: AASHTO design-vehicle dimensions for a passenger car (width 1.8 m) against a standard lane width of 3.6 m

params.name: p.yield_block_reach
params.convention: Obstruction reach: the longitudinal distance ahead of a road user, between the two reference points and taken in that road user's own frame, within which another body standing in its line of travel is a body in its way. It is taken from the length of a passenger-car design vehicle together with the gap a vehicle leaves when it is brought to a halt short of an obstruction, so that a body stopped or crossing immediately in front is covered and one further down the road is not. It names where a body stands in another's way and states no standard of conduct and no required separation.
params.source: Design-vehicle geometry: a passenger-car design vehicle of about 5.8 m with a halting gap of about 2 m between bodies, measured between reference points.

params.name: p.yield_giveway_decel
params.convention: Give-way deceleration: the magnitude of longitudinal deceleration at or above which a road user's slowing counts as giving way to another rather than as the ordinary adjustment of speed in a stream of traffic. It is taken from the comfortable deceleration of an unhurried driver, well below the braking deceleration of a stopping-sight-distance model, so that a vehicle braking for a body that has moved into its path is covered and a vehicle easing off is not. It names when a slowing shows that precedence was taken and states no standard of conduct.
params.source: Comfortable-deceleration convention (about 1.5 m/s²), set below the 3.4 m/s² braking deceleration of the stopping-sight-distance model.

params.name: p.path_conflict_reach
params.convention: Junction path-conflict convention: the distance ahead of a road user, taken along the direction its body points, within which another body standing in its line of travel obstructs its passage, so that it cannot proceed past. It is taken from the length of a passenger-car design vehicle together with the ground such a vehicle covers while its driver reacts at the speed traffic crosses a junction. It names where one body stands in another's way and states no standard of conduct and no required separation.
params.source: AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets: passenger-car design vehicle length (about 5.8 m), with the perception-reaction allowance at a low junction crossing speed.

params.name: p.stop_approach_window
params.convention: Approach look-back in time: the stretch of time behind a vehicle's entry into an intersection within which the halt required on its approach is looked for. It covers the time a vehicle stands at such a halt together with the time it takes to cover the entrance of the junction from the place of the halt - the setback of a stop line or near-side crosswalk, the width of that crossing and the vehicle's own length - at the low speed at which a vehicle proceeds after stopping. It names only how far back the halt is sought, the halt's tie to this junction being carried by the entrance reach of the intersection region, and it sets no standard of conduct.
params.source: Junction-entrance geometry, as the entrance reach p.junction_approach_reach is taken, divided by the departure speed of a vehicle proceeding from a stop, with an allowance for the time spent standing at the halt.

params.name: p.intersection_edge_tolerance
params.convention: Nearest-point tolerance: the ground distance from an intersection region within which a halted vehicle counts as standing at the point nearest that intersection, the nearest place at which it can stand without entering it. It covers the survey tolerance of the intersection's mapped boundary, the resolution of a stopped body's outline, and the small gap a driver leaves short of the edge of a junction. It names where a halt counts as made at the nearest point and states no standard of conduct and no required separation.
params.source: Mapped-boundary survey tolerance for an intersection region together with the clearance a vehicle is brought to rest short of a junction edge; well below the setback of a stop line, which is the stopping place the earlier limb reads.

_fields.aggregates: optional operator overrides only: word, classes (ru.* ids or other words). The run derives every aggregate the laws use from the corpus definitions (results/<run>/reading.json, for review); an operator entry here takes precedence over the derived one.
